doc.title: Eddie Bert interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

title: The three-trombone group with Bill Harris
summary: The 1949 Chicago engagement with Bill Harris, Milt Gold and a rhythm section.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: I mean that was one of the greatest.
We’ll get to that. I’m going to get to that. Because I wanted to ask you, you eventually hooked up again, I guess I’m going backwards now, with Bill Harris.
That was ’49. They’ve got a different date on there.

It was ’49. And we went to Chicago for three weeks. We had three trombones and rhythm. The rhythm was Shelly Manne, Bob Carter on bass and Lou Levy on piano. Bill Harris, me and Milty Gold. So we played for three weeks there. And then Mildred Bailey was supposed to join us and she was sick or something so there was a gap of like three or four weeks. And we were booked in Birdland. But everybody says man, what are we going to do for three or four weeks, just hang out? So everybody went with different bands.
